<!-- Generated by `pnpm exec nx run shared-events:schema-export` from libs/shared/events. Do not edit by hand. -->

An event records something that happened in QAuth: a sign-in, a refused token request, a new
client. Events exist so that automation outside QAuth can act on them
([ADR-018 §3](/reference/records/adr/018-1-0-scope-and-stability/)). ADR-018 names four routes
for them: signed webhooks in the Standard Webhooks format, a cursor-based event API, Shared Signals
Framework streams, and OpenTelemetry export. Every route carries the same event, in the envelope
below. The event types and their payload schemas are part of the 1.0 stability contract (ADR-018
§5).

This page is generated from the type registry in `libs/shared/events`, together with the JSON
Schema files it links.

## The envelope

Every event has these members. `type`, `category` and `data` depend on the type; the
others mean the same for every type. A member that does not apply is absent, never `null`.

```json
{
  "id": "0199f2b4-7c3e-7a51-9d2b-3a6c8e1f0a42",
  "type": "urn:qauth:event:user.signed_in:v1-rc.0",
  "time": "2026-10-22T09:30:00.123Z",
  "realm": "0199f2b4-1a2b-7c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "category": "user",
  "actor": {
    "type": "user",
    "id": "0199f2b4-2b3c-7d4e-9f5a-6b7c8d9e0f1a"
  },
  "subject": {
    "type": "user",
    "id": "0199f2b4-2b3c-7d4e-9f5a-6b7c8d9e0f1a"
  },
  "client": {
    "id": "notes-app"
  },
  "request": {
    "traceId": "req-7f3a",
    "ip": "203.0.113.7",
    "userAgent": "Mozilla/5.0"
  },
  "data": {
    "method": "password"
  }
}
```

| Member                  | Type                                                                | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                    | UUID                                                                | yes      | The event id, a UUIDv7. One event keeps one id on every route and every retry, so a receiver drops duplicates by it. It is the `webhook-id` of a webhook and the source of an SSF `jti`.                                                                              |
| `type`                  | string                                                              | yes      | The event type, `urn:qauth:event:<name>:v<N>`, or `:v<N>-rc.<M>` for a release candidate. The registry lists every type.                                                                                                                                              |
| `time`                  | time (RFC 3339, UTC)                                                | yes      | When the event happened, as an RFC 3339 time in UTC. Not when it was delivered.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `realm`                 | UUID                                                                | yes      | The id of the realm the event happened in.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `category`              | one of `user`, `admin`                                              | yes      | `user`: an end user's own activity. `admin`: an administrator's change. Fixed by the type.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `actor`                 | object                                                              | no       | Who or what caused the event.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `actor.type`            | one of `user`, `client`, `system`, `operator_cli`, or a later value | yes      | `user`: a person, signed in. `client`: an OAuth client acting for itself or, with `delegationChain`, as an agent for the subject. `system`: QAuth itself, such as a scheduled job. `operator_cli`: an operator on the server host, through a QAuth command-line tool. |
| `actor.id`              | string                                                              | no       | The actor's identifier: a user id, a client's `client_id`, or the operating-system user for `operator_cli`. Absent for `system`.                                                                                                                                      |
| `actor.delegationChain` | array of string                                                     | no       | The RFC 8693 `act` chain of a delegated request, as `client_id` values: the acting agent first, then each earlier actor. Absent when nothing was delegated.                                                                                                           |
| `subject`               | object                                                              | no       | What the event is about.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `subject.type`          | one of `user`, `client`, `api_key`, `ssf_stream`, or a later value  | yes      | What kind of thing the subject is.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `subject.id`            | string                                                              | yes      | The subject's identifier: a user id, a client's `client_id`, an API key id or a Shared Signals Framework `stream_id`. It stays valid after the subject is deleted.                                                                                                    |
| `client`                | object                                                              | no       | The OAuth client the request came through.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `client.id`             | string                                                              | yes      | The client's `client_id`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `request`               | object                                                              | no       | The HTTP request that caused the event.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `request.traceId`       | string                                                              | no       | The id under which QAuth logged the request: the `trace_id` of a problem document from the same request.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `request.ip`            | IPv4 address or IPv6 address                                        | no       | The end user's IP address, as QAuth derived it from the request. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address is written in its IPv4 form.                                                                                                                                             |
| `request.userAgent`     | string                                                              | no       | The `User-Agent` header, cut to 1024 characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `data`                  | object                                                              | yes      | The type's own payload. Its schema is the type's.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

- The `id` is a UUIDv7, assigned once when the event is recorded. A retry, a redelivery and
  every route repeat it, so a receiver drops duplicates by it. A webhook's `webhook-id` header is
  the event id, and an SSF Security Event Token's `jti` is derived from it.
- The `subject` is a plain id with no database link: it stays valid after the user or the client
  is deleted.
- A webhook body is the envelope. Standard Webhooks recommends a full-stop delimited `type`, a
  `timestamp` and `data`: the short name in the middle of the identifier is the delimited type,
  and `time` is the timestamp.
- The envelope's schema is [envelope.json](/schemas/events/envelope.json).

## Payload rules

These rules hold for every event's `data`. They were written for the audit log
([ADR-011 §8](/reference/records/adr/011-enterprise-managed-authorization/),
[ADR-017 §11](/reference/records/adr/017-first-party-login/)) and apply to events.

1. **Ids, not names or addresses.** `data` names a user, a client or a record by its id. A type
   that needs a name, an email address, a phone number or an IP address declares that field in
   its registry entry. No type registered today does.
2. **Never a secret.** No password, code, OTP, token, key, assertion, signature, cookie, secret,
   or set-up or reset link, in any form. There is no exception. An admin event's diff shows a
   changed resource's own fields; there a secret field holds `***`, never its value.
3. **Hidden identifiers are keyed HMACs.** An identifier that must not be revealed, such as the
   address a failed sign-in typed, is carried as an HMAC under a server-side key, never as the
   value and never as a plain hash.

A scanner enforces the rules. The registry's tests fail when a type's schema declares a field
named like a secret, or like personal data the type has not declared. `parseEvent`, the check a
single event passes before it is stored or sent, applies them again: a field named like a secret,
or a value shaped like a token or a key, refuses the event. The scanner reads names, so a field that holds an
id, a type or a count of such a thing passes when its name ends in `Id`, `Type` or `Count`
(`apiKeyId`, `issuedTokenType`).

## Admin events

An admin event records a change an administrator, a service account or an operator made
([ADR-020 §3](/reference/records/adr/020-ui-surfaces-and-acceptance-criteria/),
[ADR-019 Decision 7](/reference/records/adr/019-deployment-topology-and-trust-boundaries/)). Admin
events are always on: no environment key and no realm setting turns them off. Each is written in
the transaction of the change it records, so the change and its event commit together.

**The diff.** `data.diff` lists what the operation changed, one entry per field:

- `path` names the field, as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the changed resource, such as
  `/smtp/host`.
- `before` and `after` hold its value. `before` is absent when the field did not exist, and
  `after` when it no longer does; `null` means the field held `null`.
- Only changed fields are listed. A nested object present on both sides is diffed member by
  member. Any other value, an array included, is shown whole.

```json
[
  { "path": "/displayName", "before": "Notes", "after": "Team notes" },
  { "path": "/smtp/password", "before": "***", "after": "***" },
  { "path": "/allowedScopes", "before": ["openid"], "after": ["openid", "profile"] }
]
```

**Masking.** A secret field holds `***` on both sides, whatever its value. A field is secret
when the operation marks it, or when its name holds a secret, marked or not: a password, pass,
PIN, secret, token, key, salt, pepper, cookie, signature, credential, `auth` or connection string,
a key-encryption or data-encryption key (`kek`, `dek`), a set-up, reset or other one-time link,
or a one-time password's link (`totpUri`). A name whose last word only describes the secret is
shown: `accessTokenTtl`, `tokenEndpointAuthMethod`, `signingKeyId`, `jwksUri`, `keyUse`,
`saltRounds`, `authServer`. So is a code or a key that only names something: `countryCode`,
`attrKey`. A changed secret is still listed, so a rotation shows as `***` to `***`. A flag
(`true` or `false`) is never masked.

A value shaped like a secret is masked wherever it sits: a token, a signed or encrypted object, a
PEM block, an `Authorization` header value, a private or symmetric JWK, or a URL that carries a
credential: one with a password (or, over HTTP, a user name), a query or fragment member named like
a secret (`?access_token=`, `?sig=`, `?key=`, `?code=`), an `otpauth://` URI, or a webhook URL
that holds its secret in the path. A public JWK is shown, and a list of keys shows its public keys
with each private one masked. A member name shaped like a secret refuses the event.

The field names in a diff are the resource's own, so the payload scanner reads a diff's values,
not its names, and checks instead that every field named like a secret holds `***`. A diff may
show personal data, such as a contact address an admin changed: admin events are read by the
realm's admins.

**Approvals.** `data.approvals` lists the approvals the operation ran on: both approvals of a
two-admin operation, each with the approver, the passkey credential it was given with, and who
created the approver's account.

**The hash chain.** The event store chains a realm's admin events: each stores the hash of the one
before it, and its own hash is SHA-256 over the chain format's id (`qauth-event-chain/1-rc.0`,
a release candidate until 1.0.0), that hash, the id of the transaction that wrote the event, and
the event's canonical JSON (RFC 8785). A changed event breaks the chain at that event,
and a removed one at the event after it. The chain's hashes are stored beside the event and are
not part of the envelope.

## Versioning

An event type's identifier is `urn:qauth:event:<name>:v<N>`. The `<name>` is its short
name: lower-case `snake_case` segments joined by full stops, the resource first. `<N>` is the
major version of its `data`. Every QAuth-defined identifier carries a version (ADR-018 §5).

**Release candidates.** Until QAuth 1.0.0, every type is a release candidate and its identifier
ends in `-rc.<M>`, as in `urn:qauth:event:user.signed_in:v1-rc.0`. Nothing about a candidate
is promised. A breaking change before 1.0.0 raises `<M>` (`:v1-rc.0` becomes `:v1-rc.1`), so
an identifier never names two different schemas. The release that ships QAuth 1.0.0 drops the
suffix from every type: `:v1` is the version under the stability promise, and the rules below
apply from then on.

Within a major release, the contract changes only by addition:

- a new type, which is a new entry in the registry;
- a new optional member of a type's `data`, or of the envelope;
- a new value of an open set (`x-extensible-enum`, shown on this page as "or a later value").

Anything else is a breaking change: removing or renaming a member, changing its type, making a
member required, adding a required member, or narrowing what a member accepts. A breaking change
makes a new type with the next version, such as `:v2`. QAuth emits both versions for every
event until the deprecation window ends, so a receiver moves at its own pace. The old type is
marked deprecated and names its replacement. It is removed only in a new major release, no sooner
than 12 months after the deprecation (ADR-018 §5).

A receiver ignores members it does not know, and accepts a value of an open set it does not know.
The published schemas leave objects open for that reason. A closed set, such as `category`, does
not grow within a major release.

The stable-surface check compares each schema file with the last release and fails on a breaking
change that no one approved.

## Schemas

Each type has a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of its whole event: the envelope, with `type`,
`category` and `data` fixed to the type. They are served under `/schemas/events/`, and each
file's `$id` is its URL. The envelope's own schema accepts an event of any type.

### user.signed_in v1-rc.0

A person signed in: the credential checked out and QAuth started a browser session or issued tokens.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:user.signed_in:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`, when known
- Schema: [user.signed_in.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/user.signed_in.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member            | Type                                          | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `method`          | one of `password`, `wallet`, or a later value | yes      | `password`: an identifier and a password. `wallet`: a credential presented from a wallet (OpenID4VP). The set may grow in a minor release. |
| `verifierProfile` | string                                        | no       | The verifier profile the wallet presentation was checked under, such as `haip-1.0`.                                                        |

### user.sign_in_failed v1-rc.0

A sign-in was refused: an unknown identifier, a wrong credential, a locked or disabled account.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:user.sign_in_failed:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`, when known
- Schema: [user.sign_in_failed.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/user.sign_in_failed.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member            | Type                                          | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `method`          | one of `password`, `wallet`, or a later value | yes      | `password`: an identifier and a password. `wallet`: a credential presented from a wallet (OpenID4VP). The set may grow in a minor release.                                                                                     |
| `reason`          | string                                        | yes      | Why, as a `snake_case` code such as `invalid_credentials`. The set may grow in a minor release.                                                                                                                                |
| `identifierHmac`  | string                                        | no       | A keyed HMAC (HMAC-SHA-256, base64url) of the identifier the person typed, so repeated attempts at one identifier can be correlated without revealing it. Absent when the attempt named a known user, who is then the subject. |
| `verifierProfile` | string                                        | no       | The verifier profile the wallet presentation was checked under, such as `haip-1.0`.                                                                                                                                            |

### user.sign_in_step_passed v1-rc.0

The sign-in engine accepted an answer to one step of a sign-in: the identifier, or a factor that proved who the person is. A refused answer is user.sign_in_failed; the session or the tokens the sign-in leads to are user.signed_in.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:user.sign_in_step_passed:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`, when known
- Schema: [user.sign_in_step_passed.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/user.sign_in_step_passed.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member           | Type   | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `step`           | string | yes      | The step whose answer was accepted.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `identifierHmac` | string | no       | A keyed HMAC (HMAC-SHA-256, base64url) of the identifier the person typed, so repeated attempts at one identifier can be correlated without revealing it. Absent when the attempt named a known user, who is then the subject. |

### user.signed_out v1-rc.0

A person signed out, and QAuth ended their sessions.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:user.signed_out:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`, when known
- Schema: [user.signed_out.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/user.signed_out.v1-rc.0.json)
- Security type · SSF: `https://schemas.openid.net/secevent/caep/event-type/session-revoked` ([SSF events](/reference/ssf-events/))

`data` has no members: the envelope carries the event.

### user.registration_failed v1-rc.0

An account could not be created, for example because the address is in use.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:user.registration_failed:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: none: the event never carries one
- Schema: [user.registration_failed.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/user.registration_failed.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member           | Type   | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `reason`         | string | yes      | Why, as a `snake_case` code such as `invalid_credentials`. The set may grow in a minor release.                                                                                                                                |
| `identifierHmac` | string | no       | A keyed HMAC (HMAC-SHA-256, base64url) of the identifier the person typed, so repeated attempts at one identifier can be correlated without revealing it. Absent when the attempt named a known user, who is then the subject. |

### token.issued v1-rc.0

The token endpoint issued tokens: for an authorization code, a refresh, client credentials, a token exchange or a JWT bearer assertion.

| Member            | Type                                                 | Required | Meaning                                                                                                       |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `grantType`       | string                                               | yes      | The `grant_type` of the token request, such as `authorization_code`.                                          |
| `scopes`          | array of string                                      | no       | The scopes of the issued access token.                                                                        |
| `audience`        | array of string                                      | no       | The audience of the issued token.                                                                             |
| `resources`       | array of string                                      | no       | The RFC 8707 resource indicators the token is bound to.                                                       |
| `expiresIn`       | integer                                              | no       | The lifetime of the issued access token, in seconds.                                                          |
| `issuedTokenType` | string                                               | no       | The RFC 8693 `issued_token_type` of a token exchange.                                                         |
| `refreshFamilyId` | UUID                                                 | no       | The refresh family the issued refresh token belongs to. Every rotation keeps it.                              |

| `idJagId`         | string                                               | no       | The `jti` of the identity assertion authorization grant minted or consumed (ADR-011). Never the grant itself. |

### token.request_failed v1-rc.0

The token endpoint refused a request: failed client authentication, an invalid or replayed grant, a scope or resource outside what was granted.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:token.request_failed:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`, when known
- Schema: [token.request_failed.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/token.request_failed.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member                | Type    | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | ------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `grantType`           | string  | no       | The `grant_type` of the token request, such as `authorization_code`.                                                                                      |
| `error`               | string  | yes      | The OAuth or OpenID Connect `error` code the request was refused with, such as `invalid_grant`.                                                           |
| `reason`              | string  | no       | Why, as a `snake_case` code such as `invalid_credentials`. The set may grow in a minor release.                                                           |
| `refreshFamilyId`     | UUID    | no       | The refresh family a replayed grant (reason `code_replay` or `refresh_replay`) had issued, which the refusal revoked. Absent when the grant issued none.  |

### token.family_revoked v1-rc.0

A replayed grant made QAuth revoke the refresh family it had issued: an authorization code redeemed a second time, or a refresh token presented after it was rotated or revoked. Emitted only when the replay revoked refresh tokens, beside the `token.request_failed` that refused it.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:token.family_revoked:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `critical` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`, when known

| Member                | Type                                                     | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `reason`              | one of `code_replay`, `refresh_replay`, or a later value | yes      | `code_replay`: an authorization code redeemed a second time. `refresh_replay`: a refresh token presented after it was rotated or revoked. The set may grow in a minor release. |
| `refreshFamilyId`     | UUID                                                     | yes      | The refresh family that was revoked.                                                                                                                                           |
| `revokedRefreshCount` | integer                                                  | yes      | How many refresh tokens of the family were revoked, at least 1.                                                                                                                |

### client.first_party_changed v1-rc.0

An operator set, changed or removed a client's first-party profile (ADR-017 Decision 2), its policy or its written reason. Removing the profile revoked every refresh token family of the client in the same transaction.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:client.first_party_changed:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `admin` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `client`, when known
- Schema: [client.first_party_changed.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/client.first_party_changed.v1-rc.0.json)
- Security type · SSF: none ([SSF events](/reference/ssf-events/))

| Member              | Type                                                             | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `from`              | one of `web_redirect`, `native_backend`, or a later value or any | yes      | `web_redirect` or `native_backend`: the profile before the change, or `null` when the client was not first party. The set may grow in a minor release.                                                      |
| `to`                | one of `web_redirect`, `native_backend`, or a later value or any | yes      | The profile after the change, or `null` when it was removed. The set may grow in a minor release.                                                                                                           |
| `flows`             | array of one of `login`, `register`, `reset`, or a later value   | no       | A `native_backend` client's flows after the change: `login`, `register`, `reset`. Absent for any other profile.                                                                                             |
| `pkceRequired`      | boolean                                                          | no       | Whether a `native_backend` client's policy requires PKCE at the authorization challenge endpoint after the change. `false` is a deviation the operator chose for this client. Absent for any other profile. |
| `writtenReason`     | string                                                           | no       | The reason the operator wrote for the profile, as stored with the client. Absent when the profile was removed.                                                                                              |
| `revokedTokenCount` | integer                                                          | yes      | How many refresh tokens the removal revoked: every token of every family of the client that was not already revoked, expired ones included. `0` when the profile was set or changed.                        |

The OpenID4VP response endpoint accepted a wallet presentation. This is not a sign-in: the flow that asked for it decides.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:wallet.presentation_received:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: none: the event never carries one
- Schema: [wallet.presentation_received.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/wallet.presentation_received.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member              | Type    | Required | Meaning                                                                             |
| ------------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `verifierProfile`   | string  | yes      | The verifier profile the wallet presentation was checked under, such as `haip-1.0`. |
| `presentationCount` | integer | yes      | How many presentations the response held.                                           |

### interaction.created v1-rc.0

A browser ceremony began: the server created an interaction and bound it to the browser that started it with a flow cookie.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:interaction.created:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`, when known
- Schema: [interaction.created.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/interaction.created.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member        | Type                                     | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `interaction` | UUID                                     | yes      | The interaction: a random reference the server gave it, which links the events of one interaction. Never the interaction id the browser holds. |
| `purpose`     | one of `authorization`, or a later value | yes      | `authorization`: an authorization request at the authorization endpoint. The set may grow in a minor release.                                  |
| `step`        | string                                   | yes      | The first step the ceremony asks for.                                                                                                          |
| `replaces`    | UUID                                     | no       | For an interaction that a user switch started: the interaction it replaces, which ended with it. Nothing proved in that one carries over.      |

### interaction.answered v1-rc.0

The engine processed an answer to the current step of an interaction. Of two answers to one step, only the one processed is recorded.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:interaction.answered:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`, when known
- Schema: [interaction.answered.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/interaction.answered.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member        | Type                                                              | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `interaction` | UUID                                                              | yes      | The interaction: a random reference the server gave it, which links the events of one interaction. Never the interaction id the browser holds.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `step`        | string                                                            | yes      | The step the answer was for.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `outcome`     | one of `next_step`, `authenticated`, `finished`, or a later value | yes      | `next_step`: another step comes next, or the same one again after a refused answer. `authenticated`: the answer proved who the user is; the browser session and the flow cookie were replaced. `finished`: the interaction ended, and the request it was for is completed. The set may grow in a minor release. |

### interaction.cancelled v1-rc.0

An interaction ended before it finished, at the request of the browser that started it.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:interaction.cancelled:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`, when known
- Schema: [interaction.cancelled.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/interaction.cancelled.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member        | Type                                           | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `interaction` | UUID                                           | yes      | The interaction: a random reference the server gave it, which links the events of one interaction. Never the interaction id the browser holds.                                    |
| `step`        | string                                         | yes      | The step the interaction was at.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `reason`      | one of `user`, `user_switch`, or a later value | yes      | `user`: the person cancelled. `user_switch`: the person chose another account, and a new interaction for the same request replaced this one. The set may grow in a minor release. |

### interaction.expired v1-rc.0

An interaction expired before it finished or was cancelled: it reached its absolute expiry, or its first step went unanswered for too long. It can no longer be read or answered.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:interaction.expired:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`, when known
- Schema: [interaction.expired.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/interaction.expired.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member        | Type   | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `interaction` | UUID   | yes      | The interaction: a random reference the server gave it, which links the events of one interaction. Never the interaction id the browser holds. |
| `step`        | string | no       | The step the interaction was at, when the server still had its record. Absent otherwise.                                                       |

### request.csrf_rejected v1-rc.0

A form post was refused because its CSRF check failed: the token was missing or did not match.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:request.csrf_rejected:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`, when known
- Schema: [request.csrf_rejected.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/request.csrf_rejected.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member | Type                                                                                                 | Required | Meaning                                                        |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `form` | one of `sign_in`, `wallet_sign_in`, `wallet_link`, `consent`, `consent_revocation`, or a later value | yes      | The form that was posted. The set may grow in a minor release. |

### ssf.stream.verification_requested v1-rc.0

A receiver asked for a verification event on one of its Shared Signals Framework streams (SSF 1.0 §8.1.4). QAuth sends the verification Security Event Token to that stream only.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:ssf.stream.verification_requested:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `ssf_stream`, when known
- Schema: [ssf.stream.verification_requested.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/ssf.stream.verification_requested.v1-rc.0.json)

| Member  | Type   | Required | Meaning                                                                                                 |
| ------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `state` | string | no       | The opaque value the receiver sent, returned to it in the verification event. Absent when it sent none. |

### key.emergency_retired v1-rc.0

An operator retired a published key of the realm that may be compromised (ADR-019 Decision 9): it left the JWKS at once, no verifier in the auth server accepts it, and a new key took its place. A key QAuth does not publish, such as the data-at-rest key, is not recorded as this type.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:key.emergency_retired:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `admin` · Severity: `critical` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: none: the event never carries one
- Schema: [key.emergency_retired.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/key.emergency_retired.v1-rc.0.json)
- Security type · SSF: `urn:qauth:secevent:key-emergency-retired:v1-rc.0` ([SSF events](/reference/ssf-events/))

| Member    | Type                                                                                                                                                                                | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `keyId`   | string                                                                                                                                                                              | yes      | The `kid` of the retired key. Never the key itself.                                                                                                    |
| `purpose` | one of `token_signing`, `event_signing`, `federation_entity`, `trust_anchor`, `oid4vp_request_signing`, `oid4vp_response_encryption`, `upstream_client_assertion`, or a later value | yes      | What the key was for, one of the purposes whose keys QAuth publishes, such as `token_signing` or `event_signing`. The set may grow in a minor release. |

### admin.change_applied v1-rc.0

An administrator, a service account or an operator changed something in the realm through an admin operation. Emitted for every such change, in its transaction; no setting turns it off. The admin events of a realm form one hash chain.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:admin.change_applied:v1-rc.0`
- Category: `admin` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: none: the event never carries one
- Schema: [admin.change_applied.v1-rc.0.json](/schemas/events/admin.change_applied.v1-rc.0.json)
- Diff: `data.diff` lists what changed, with every secret value masked ([Admin events](#admin-events))

| Member        | Type            | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | --------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `operation`   | string          | yes      | The operation's id in the permission catalog, such as `realms.policies.write` (ADR-019 Decision 7).                                                                                                                    |
| `target`      | object          | yes      | What the operation changed.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `target.type` | string          | yes      | What kind of thing the operation changed, as a `snake_case` code such as `realm`, `client` or `webhook_subscription`. The set grows with the admin API.                                                                |
| `target.id`   | string          | yes      | The changed thing's identifier, such as a realm id or a `client_id`. It stays valid after the thing is deleted.                                                                                                        |
| `diff`        | array of object | yes      | What the operation changed in the target, field by field. Only changed fields are listed. A nested object is diffed member by member; any other value, an array included, is shown whole. Every secret value is `***`. |
| `approvals`   | array of object | yes      | The approvals the operation ran on, both of a two-admin operation. Empty when it needed none.                                                                                                                          |

## Earlier event names

Before the event contract, QAuth wrote free-form event names to its audit log and its log
lines. Each becomes a registered type. Several earlier names become one type, and the name implied
some `data`. Since 0.2.0 the auth server records events and writes no audit row; the upgrade
copies every audit row into the event store with this map. A copied event gets the `data` its name
implies and the members of the old row that have the declared form. A required member an old row
cannot supply gets a fixed value: `unknown` for a code, `false` for a flag, an empty list, `0`
for a count or the nil UUID for an id. Log lines keep their names.

| Earlier name                      | Written to | Type                                                   | Implied `data`                |
| --------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- |
| `user.login.success`              | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.signed_in:v1-rc.0`               | `method: password`            |
| `user.login.failure`              | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.sign_in_failed:v1-rc.0`          | `method: password`            |
| `ui.login.success`                | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.signed_in:v1-rc.0`               | `method: password`            |
| `ui.login.failure`                | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.sign_in_failed:v1-rc.0`          | `method: password`            |
| `ui.login.csrf_failure`           | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:request.csrf_rejected:v1-rc.0`        | `form: sign_in`               |
| `ui.wallet_login.success`         | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.signed_in:v1-rc.0`               | `method: wallet`              |
